purpose: Change a combined-length requirement and follow one ordered pair into a binary relation and its complete membership count.
meaning: A predicate takes a stated number of arguments and yields a truth value. A binary relation on a domain is a set of ordered pairs; its membership predicate tests two arguments. The two-strip example distinguishes the truth of one pair from the number of all pairs satisfying the same rule.

definition.setting: A binary length relation on two independent copies of one six-element domain.
conditions: There are two independent strip supplies, each offering lengths 2,4,6,8,10 and 12 cm. A left choice and a right choice form an ordered pair (x,y). Equal lengths are allowed.
The domain product D×D contains 36 ordered choices. The choices (6,8) and (8,6) are distinct even though their sums are equal.
The free requirement h ranges from zero to 26 cm. Membership means x+y≥h, with equality included.
The relation Rₕ contains pairs, Rₕ(x,y) states one pair’s membership truth, and |Rₕ| is an integer count. A unary predicate such as x≥h has one argument and is a different test.
definition.domain_notes: Both argument positions range over the stated finite domain. Changing h changes the relation on that fixed domain product. A count of satisfying choices is not a probability unless an additional sampling model is supplied.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original restricted-family arguments; independent review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: Choose a left length x and a right length y independently from D={2,4,6,8,10,12} cm. The predicate Rₕ(x,y) is true exactly when x+y≥h. The relation Rₕ is the set of satisfying ordered pairs; |Rₕ| counts those pairs. The highlighted pair is (6,8), with total 14 cm.
grammar.precedence: Form an ordered pair, add its two lengths, and compare the sum with h before counting its membership.
